newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks resist profit-taking, end higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks resist profit-taking, end higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Tuesday, with the market showing resilience as some investors took profits this session, analysts said.

The Hang Seng index rose 18.79 points to 11,921.22, another 31-month closing high. The blue chip index hit an intra-day 1996 high of 11,930.16 and a session low of 11,857.43. Turnover was HK$6.06 billion compared to Monday's HK$5.96 billion.
"It is acting very well considering the sharp rise we've had," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
"We have been acting like a bull market where surprises tend to be on the upside," he added.
Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia, said some investors had been selling into strength on Tuesday. "But there are people the other way too," he said.
"I think there is still a fair undertone. There is still quite a bit of buying. People are taking advantage of liquidity in the market to place their bets," said Lesko.
October Hang Seng futures rose 35 points to 11,875.
Gorges said the Hang Seng index was likely to post further gains before consolidating. "There is a bit of overseas buying around and it looks like will go higher before consolidating."
"I would have thought that 12,000 to 12,200 is the area where it is likely to meet more resistance and need a proper breather before moving forward," said Gorges.
Hang Seng Bank closed at a new all-time high of HK$83.25, up HK$1.25, buoyed by U.S. interest.

"When big funds want to get into the market they buy banks which are leaders. The leadership in the market shows there is fund money coming in. It just wants in and is not shopping around for value," said Gorges.
Bank of East Asis rose HK$0.40 to HK$28.85 and HSBC Holdings ended the session steady at HK$143.50.
Conglomerates Swire Pacific and Wheelock fell. Swire ended off HK$1.25 at HK$68.00 and Wheelock shed HK$0.15 to HK$16.95.
Sun Hung Kai Properties is due to release its final results on Wednesday. The stock rose HK$0.25 to HK$82.50.
Sino Land was due to release its 1995/96 results after the market close and ended the session steady at HK$8.45.
Dransfield shares resumed trading on Tuesday after Monday's suspension and rose HK$0.175 to HK$0.65 after the company announced a share placement plan.
